Washington County by the numbers

Where is Washington County, Utah?

Washington County fills the southwest corner of Utah, with Arizona to the south and Nevada to the west. It covers 2,430 square miles, almost all of it land, and St. George has been the county seat since 1856.

Iron County lies to the north, Kane County to the east, Mohave County in Arizona to the south and Lincoln County in Nevada to the west. Three regions meet here: the Colorado Plateau, the Great Basin and the Mojave Desert. The territorial legislature created the county on March 3, 1852, and its lines have not changed since March 10, 1892.

Utah's lowest elevation is in this county, at Beaver Dam Wash (2,178 feet). The highest is Signal Peak in the Pine Valley Mountains at 10,369 feet. Part of Zion National Park, three state parks and the Red Cliffs National Conservation Area also fall inside the county.

The area was settled in the 1850s and 1860s as a cotton mission, which is why it earned the nickname "Utah's Dixie." The Silver Reef mining town began in 1875 and was abandoned by 1891. St. George itself was founded in 1861 and incorporated on January 17, 1862.

What do the Washington County numbers show?

Washington County is one of the fastest-growing counties in Utah, and the figures below show the pace. They come from the Wikipedia county page, which relies on Census Bureau data and a 2025 estimate.

MeasureFigure

Growth 2010 to 202030.5%
Households (2020)62,416
Owner-occupied householdsabout 73.0%

Roughly 26.4% of residents were under 18 and 22.1% were 65 or older in 2020.

Which cities and towns make up the county?

St. George is the largest city, and a dozen or more smaller communities surround it. St. George had 95,342 residents in 2020 and a 2024 estimate of 106,288, which makes it the largest city in Utah outside the Wasatch Front.

  • Santa Clara and Ivins sit west of St. George.
  • Washington lies east of St. George, and Hurricane and La Verkin are farther east.
  • Toquerville, Virgin, Springdale and Rockville are smaller communities in the east of the county, near Zion.
  • Enterprise, New Harmony, Hildale, Gunlock, Veyo and Pine Valley are smaller places in the north and west.

Wikipedia lists more than 20 neighborhoods inside St. George, among them Bloomington, Little Valley, Southgate, Sunbrook, The Ledges, Desert Color and Stone Cliff. Name the neighborhood when you describe your property to anyone who is valuing it.

What does the desert climate and flood history mean for a house?

Heat and occasional flooding are the two weather facts that affect a Washington County house most. St. George has a July mean daily high of 101.9 degrees, about 60 afternoons a year above 100, and only about 8.8 inches of rain annually.

Monsoon thunderstorms arrive from early July to mid-September. Water has done real damage here: after 44 days of rain in early 1862, floods nearly destroyed St. George, Washington, Santa Clara and Grafton. In January 2005, a flood along the Santa Clara River destroyed 28 homes and killed one person.

Higher country behaves differently. Pine Valley often gets more than 20 inches of precipitation a year, and the north end of the county is semi-arid. For a seller, a cooling system near the end of its life and any house close to a wash or river are the points a buyer is likely to question.

What drives the Washington County economy?

Tourism, construction, health care and retirement living carry the economy. Zion National Park is a major draw, and most of the income in Springdale and Rockville comes from visitors.

St. George has over a dozen golf courses and many seasonal vacation-home owners. SkyWest Airlines is headquartered there, and St. George Regional Hospital is described as the only 24-hour trauma center between Las Vegas and the Wasatch Front. Utah Tech University had 12,567 students in 2023 to 2024.

The Washington County School District covers the whole county. St. George Regional Airport, in the southeast of the city, had nonstop service to Salt Lake City, Denver, Phoenix, Los Angeles and Dallas-Fort Worth as of 2023. Wikipedia notes that large irrigated farms in eastern St. George and Washington have been sold for housing and commercial lots.

Which Washington County offices handle property tax?

The treasurer bills and collects, and the auditor takes valuation appeals. Both work from 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George, UT 84770.

OfficeRolePhone
TreasurerTax notices, payments, delinquent taxes(435) 301-7720
AuditorBoard of Equalization, Tax Commission appeal forms(435) 301-7220
County AdministrationGeneral county contact(435) 301-7000

The treasurer's FAQ says real property tax is due November 30 every year, even if you never received a notice. The county sends a notice to each owner and sends payment information to the mortgage company, but owners are expected to check the notice for errors. If your neighbors got a notice and you did not, call or email the treasurer for a copy.

How does Washington County treat partial and late payments?

Partial payments of $10 or more per parcel are accepted at any time. Each payment is applied first to interest, then to penalty, then to tax. When more than one year is delinquent, the most recent year is paid first, as Utah law requires.

The treasurer does not offer payment plans for delinquent taxes. Each May, the clerk-auditor holds a sale of properties that have been delinquent for at least five years, with notice in a newspaper about four weeks beforehand. Utah law does not allow tax liens or tax lien certificates to be sold.

Tax relief programs run through the clerk-auditor, including exemptions for the blind and for disabled veterans, a circuit breaker program, and indigent and hardship abatements.

How do you appeal a Washington County property value?

Ask the Board of Equalization to review your value. By statute, the deadline is the later of September 15 or 45 days after the county auditor gives notice, and the board must rule within 60 days of the application.

A valid application includes your own estimate of fair market value and any evidence that your assessment is out of line with comparable homes. The county's page announces when each year's window has closed, so check the auditor's appeal page early in the season rather than in mid-September.

If you disagree with the board, file Form TC-194 with the county auditor no later than 30 days after the Notice of Determination. The auditor forwards it to the Utah State Tax Commission.

What should you do about property tax when selling in Washington County?

Property tax follows the house, not the seller. The treasurer explains that the tax is a lien against the property, and that when a house changes hands mid-year the title company prorates it at closing.

Your settlement statement shows the split, so read it line by line.

  • Find your parcel in the county's tax notice search at outpost.washco.utah.gov.
  • Confirm whether a lender escrow paid this year's bill.
  • Ask the treasurer to confirm any back balance before closing.
  • Update your mailing address so later notices do not land in an empty house.

Inherited houses, vacation homes and rentals in St. George and Hurricane are the situations we hear about most, and we buy Washington County houses as-is.

More questions about Washington County, UT Property Tax Guide

When are Washington County, Utah property taxes due?

Real property tax is due November 30 every year, even if you did not receive a notice. The treasurer accepts partial payments of $10 or more per parcel at any time. The office is at 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George.

How do I appeal my Washington County property value?

File an application with the county Board of Equalization by the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor gives notice. Include your own value estimate and comparable evidence. The auditor's office at (435) 301-7220 can confirm the current year's window.

What if I disagree with the Board of Equalization decision?

Appeal to the Utah State Tax Commission with Form TC-194, filed with the county auditor within 30 days after the Notice of Determination.

Does Washington County sell tax liens?

No. Utah law does not allow tax liens or lien certificates to be sold. Instead, the clerk-auditor holds a sale each May for properties delinquent at least five years.

Who pays the property tax when a Washington County house sells?

The title company prorates the tax at closing, and your settlement statement shows the split. We buy houses as-is in Washington County and can work with whatever tax balance is owed.

Salt Lake County by the numbers

What is Salt Lake County, Utah, and how is it laid out?

Salt Lake County is Utah's most populous county and holds the state capital, Salt Lake City, as its county seat. The county was organized on January 31, 1850, and the 2020 census counted 1,185,238 residents, with a 2025 estimate of 1,220,916.

It covers 807 square miles, of which 742 are land, and it fills the Salt Lake Valley between the Wasatch Range on the east and the Oquirrh Mountains on the west. The Jordan River runs north through the valley and the Great Salt Lake borders the northwest corner.

Cities in the county include West Valley City, West Jordan, South Jordan, Sandy, Murray, Draper, Herriman, Riverton, Midvale, Taylorsville, Holladay, Millcreek, Cottonwood Heights, Bluffdale and South Salt Lake, along with unincorporated Magna, Kearns and Copperton. Each of these sits in the same county tax system, so the dates and offices below apply across them.

What shapes the Salt Lake County economy?

The county's gross domestic product reached $153.846 billion in 2024, and its economy has long mixed services, mining, defense and health care. The Bingham Canyon Mine is among the largest open-pit mines in the world, Northrop Grumman builds solid rocket motors in Magna, and the University of Utah, Intermountain Health Care and University of Utah Healthcare are among the biggest employers.

Winter sports have mattered since Alta Ski Area opened in 1939. Salt Lake City International Airport is a hub for Delta and SkyWest, TRAX light rail runs three lines, and FrontRunner commuter rail links Ogden to Provo. Interstates 15, 80 and 215 cross the valley. For a seller, proximity to rail and the freeway grid is a usable talking point.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Salt Lake County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What does the Salt Lake County climate and geology mean for a home?

The valley is dry, averaging about 15 inches of precipitation a year, but it gets roughly 55 inches of snow, and winter temperature inversions trap pollution on the valley floor. Heavier snow falls on the benches, up to about 100 inches.

The Wasatch Fault runs along the mountain front. It is about 240 miles long, roughly 80% of Utah's people live along it, and one source gives a 57% chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger earthquake within 50 years. Buyers and inspectors may ask about it. If your house has had foundation repair, a chimney fix or a retrofit, keep the paperwork in one folder.

Which Salt Lake County offices handle what?

Several county offices touch a property sale. The Assessor appraises property as of January 1 and completes the assessment roll by May 22, and the Auditor mails Notices of Valuation and Tax Change around July 22. The offices below handle billing, recording and appeals.

OfficeWhat it doesContact
TreasurerBills and collects tax, runs tax relief2001 S State St, Suite N1-200; 385-468-8300; treasurer@saltlakecounty.gov
RecorderRecords deeds and other documents2001 S State St, Suite N1-600; 385-468-8145
Board of EqualizationHears value appeals2002 S State St, #N3-300; PO Box 144575

The Treasurer's office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and its tax relief division answers at 385-468-8300, option 2.

What are the key Salt Lake County property tax dates?

The main deadline is November 30, the last day to pay the current year's property tax without a penalty. If it falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day. Official tax notices must be mailed by November 1.

  • January 1: the Assessor appraises property and establishes ownership.
  • Around July 22: valuation notices go out.
  • August 1: the appeal window at the Board of Equalization opens.
  • September 15: the appeal window closes, or 45 days after the notice, whichever is later.
  • December 1: unpaid tax becomes delinquent.
  • January 31: the penalty rises if the balance is still unpaid.

The delinquency penalty on December 1 is the greater of 2.5% or $10 per parcel. It drops to the greater of 1% or $10 if you pay in full by January 31. After that, the penalty returns to 2.5% plus interest retroactive to January 1. A seller who closes in December or January should ask the title company whether the bill is paid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Salt Lake County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does the residential exemption work when a house changes hands?

Utah taxes a qualifying primary home on 55% of its market value because of a 45% residential exemption. The Utah State Tax Commission says the home must be occupied as a primary domicile for at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, by the owner or a full-time tenant, and a household may claim only one.

The exemption does not move to a new owner automatically. The buyer files a new declaration, which Form TC-473A covers starting January 1, 2027, and the application is due to the Board of Equalization by September 15. A late or missing filing can leave the house taxed at 100% of market value for that year. If you are selling, tell your buyer about this step.

How do you appeal a Salt Lake County valuation?

You appeal to the county Board of Equalization, and the 2026 deadline is September 15. In-person filings must arrive by 5:00 p.m. that day, mailed filings must be postmarked by then, and online filings must be finished by 11:59 p.m.

  • Email the signed application and all evidence to propertytaxappeals@saltlakecounty.gov, or mail it to the Board at 2002 S State St #N3-300.
  • Useful evidence includes at least three recent comparable sales, a professional appraisal, documented errors in county records, and your own purchase documents.
  • If you bought between July 1 of the prior year and June 30 of the current year, the closing statement is often strong evidence.

Independent hearing officers review the evidence and recommend a decision, and the Board decides whether the value goes up, goes down or stays. The county says to pay the bill by the due date even if the appeal is pending, because refunds come only after a final decision. A county Board decision can be appealed to the State Tax Commission within 30 days.

What tax relief programs does the Salt Lake County Treasurer offer?

The Treasurer runs several relief programs for owners who meet age, income or status rules. Applications open January 1, and the statutory deadline is September 1.

ProgramWho qualifies
Circuit BreakerAge 67 or older, or a surviving spouse, with household income up to $44,221
Indigent ReliefAge 65 or older or receiving disability benefits, with income and assets below $44,221
Senior DeferralHomeowners age 75 or older meeting income and asset rules
Veteran ReliefVeterans with a service-related disability, or out-of-state active duty members
Blind ReliefLegally blind owners and certain survivors
Hardship ReliefExtreme hardship, subject to income and asset limits

A deferral or relief claim on a house you plan to sell affects the payoff figure, so ask the Treasurer about it early.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens if Salt Lake County property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid tax can end in a tax sale after about five years. The redemption period expires on March 15 of the fifth year after the taxes become delinquent, and the Auditor holds the final sale on the fourth Thursday of May. Owners can still pay up until the sale.

Notice runs in a newspaper for four weeks and is mailed to owners and interested parties. Ask the Treasurer for an exact payoff figure if you are in this position. A sale that closes before the redemption deadline lets escrow pay the balance out of the proceeds.

What does it take to record a deed in Salt Lake County?

The Salt Lake County Recorder charges a flat $40 per recording, and the document must meet formatting and notary rules. The Recorder's office is at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, and it is open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

  • White 8.5 by 11 inch paper, printed on one side, with black text.
  • A 2.5 by 4.5 inch blank space in the upper right corner of the first page.
  • The parcel serial number, a legal description for property in the county, and the grantee's address.
  • An original signature with a notary acknowledgment and a legible stamp.

Title companies handle this, but a deed signed outside a closing, such as one between family members, needs the same care.

More questions about Salt Lake County, UT Property Tax Guide

When are Salt Lake County property taxes due?

November 30 is the last day to pay the current year's tax without penalty. If that date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day. Unpaid tax becomes delinquent on December 1.

What is the deadline to appeal a Salt Lake County property value?

The deadline is September 15, or 45 days after the valuation notice is mailed, whichever is later. For 2026, the county set September 15 as the filing deadline. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization.

Does the Utah residential exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. The exemption does not transfer automatically, and the buyer must file a new declaration. A late or missing filing can mean taxation at 100% of market value for that year.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?

The flat recording fee is $40 per recording, with $2 more for each legal description over 10. A recorded copy costs $2 per page.

What happens to a Salt Lake County house after the redemption period?

The redemption period ends March 15 of the fifth year after the tax becomes delinquent, and the Auditor holds the tax sale in late May. You can still pay the balance until the sale takes place.

Can I get property tax relief as a senior in Salt Lake County?

Possibly. The Treasurer lists Circuit Breaker relief for ages 67 and up with income up to $44,221 and a Senior Deferral for owners 75 and older. Call 385-468-8300, option 2, to check eligibility.

Tooele County by the numbers

Where is Tooele County and how is it laid out?

Tooele County sits in northwestern Utah, west of Salt Lake County, and covers 7,286 square miles, of which 6,941 are land. That makes it the second largest county in the state, and one of the driest.

Most of the people live in a strip along the east edge. The Oquirrh Mountains separate Tooele Valley from the Salt Lake Valley, the Stansbury Mountains run parallel to them, and Rush Valley lies to the south behind a low rise called the Stockton Bar. The western half belongs to the Great Salt Lake Desert, with the Bonneville Salt Flats crossed by Interstate 80. Skull Valley, between the Cedar and Stansbury ranges, holds the Skull Valley Indian Reservation and Dugway Proving Ground.

The county borders Box Elder, Davis, Salt Lake, Utah and Juab counties in Utah, plus Elko and White Pine counties in Nevada. For a seller, the practical point is that two houses with the same Tooele County mailing address can sit in very different settings, from a town lot in Tooele to acreage on the edge of the desert, and the assessor values them separately.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tooele County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Which towns and areas make up the county?

Tooele is the county seat and the largest city, followed by Grantsville, with smaller communities such as Erda, Lake Point, Stockton, Rush Valley, Wendover and Ibapah scattered across the county.

  • Tooele: 35,742 residents in 2020, on the western slope of the Oquirrhs at about 4,915 feet. It was incorporated on June 19, 1853, and sits roughly 40 minutes from Salt Lake City.
  • Grantsville: 12,617 residents in 2020 at about 4,265 feet, incorporated January 12, 1867. State Route 138 runs through town toward Interstate 80 and east to Stansbury Park.
  • Stansbury Park: 9,851 residents in 2020, up from 5,145 in 2010. It is unincorporated, so the county provides most services, and it is about six miles north of Tooele on State Route 36.
  • Wendover: 1,115 residents in 2020, directly across the line from West Wendover, Nevada.

Stansbury Park deserves a note for sellers. It began in 1970 as a planned community with a golf course and a man-made lake, water and sewer come from the Stansbury Park Improvement District, and the Stansbury Park Community Association gives preliminary approval to housing and remodeling plans. If you own there, a buyer will ask about association rules early.

What drives the Tooele County economy?

Mining, defense and industrial work have shaped Tooele County since the 1860s, and a growing share of residents now commute to the Salt Lake Valley.

The employers named in the Tooele city entry include Kennecott Utah Copper, which runs the Bingham Canyon Mine on the far side of the Oquirrhs, US Magnesium, EnergySolutions at Clive, a Cabela's distribution center, and government at the federal, state and county level. The former Tooele Army Depot land now hosts the Tooele Industrial Depot, a group of manufacturers, warehouses and offices. Grantsville points to a new Walmart distribution center and the Utah Motorsports Campus as nearby draws.

Census yearTooele County population
195014,636
198026,033
200040,735
201058,218
202072,698

Population nearly doubled between 2000 and 2020. A 2008 CNNMoney ranking named Tooele the U.S. county with the greatest job growth since 2000.

What does the weather mean for a Tooele County house?

Tooele sees hot dry summers and cold winters with real snow, so roofs, heating systems and exterior paint take steady wear.

The Tooele climate summary lists normal highs of 38.7 degrees in January and 91.4 degrees in July, about 18.44 inches of precipitation a year and 75.3 inches of snowfall. The record high is 106 degrees and the record low is minus 16. Grantsville gets lake-effect snow from the Great Salt Lake only occasionally, and Wendover averages about 4.58 inches of precipitation, which makes it the driest spot in the Great Basin.

A buyer's inspector in this county will look first at the roof, the furnace and the water heater, then at settling and grading around the foundation. A house that has sat vacant through a few winters will show more of that wear, and selling as-is means you skip those repairs.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tooele County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What are the Tooele County property tax dates?

Tooele County values property as of January 1, mails valuation notices in July or August, and treats November 30 as the last day to pay without penalty.

WhenWhat happens
January 1Property is valued as it stood on this date
May 22Assessor completes the roll and certifies values to the Auditor
May or JuneTax sale for parcels more than five years delinquent
July or AugustValuation notices mailed
August or SeptemberBoard of Equalization window, 45 days from mailing
By November 1Property tax notices mailed
November 30Last day to pay without penalty
December 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent

The county posts these on its assessor dates page. The Treasurer's office at 47 S. Main Street in Tooele takes questions at (435) 843-3190, Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

How do you appeal a Tooele County valuation?

You have 45 days from the mailing of your Notice of Property Valuation, or until September 15, to file with the county Board of Equalization.

The county accepts four kinds of evidence, and at least one is required:

  • Recent comparable sales of similar homes that closed before January 1 for less than the assessed value.
  • A closing statement from a purchase made before January 1, with a bank-required appraisal for short sales, bank-owned sales and foreclosures.
  • An appraisal with an effective date within the year.
  • A written statement of a factual error, such as wrong square footage or a carport listed as a garage.

High taxes by themselves are not grounds, because rates come from the budget-approving cities, school districts and districts that hold public hearings. If the board's answer disappoints you, the State Tax Commission accepts a written appeal within 30 days of the board's decision, filed through the county auditor. The Tax Commission's appeals publication estimates a typical homeowner saves $4 to $8 in tax for each $1,000 of value removed.

How does the primary residential exemption affect a sale?

A qualifying primary home is taxed on 55 percent of its market value, and the exemption does not follow the house to a new owner automatically.

The county says the exemption covers up to one acre per residential unit, requires use as a primary residence, and counts part-year use of at least 183 consecutive days. Each household gets one. When a property changes hands, the new owner has to apply, using Form TC-473A emailed to assessorsurvey@tooeleco.gov. If the form does not come back within 30 days, the county sends a notice with 30 more days, and after that the exemption is removed.

The State Tax Commission adds that starting January 1, 2027, any change in ownership interest, including a deed or trust transfer, calls for a new form under 2026 SB 238, with applications due to the Board of Equalization by September 15. A lost exemption means taxation at 100 percent of market value. Heirs and landlords selling a Tooele County rental should know this before they list.

What happens when property tax goes unpaid in Tooele County?

Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, penalties and interest start to build, and a parcel can go to a tax sale once it is more than five years behind.

A Tooele Transcript Bulletin report on the 2022 cycle gives a sense of scale. Nearly $5.5 million was unpaid on December 31, 2022, and 1,946 delinquency notices went out. The penalty was the greater of 1 percent or $10 at first, rising to the greater of 2.5 percent or $10 after January 31, with interest of 10 percent on the December 1 balance. Those were the 2022 figures, so confirm current ones with the Treasurer.

The Auditor's tax sale is advertised weekly for four weeks, and owners can redeem before the sale. If you are behind on taxes and want out, call us before the delinquency list is published. We ask the Treasurer for the payoff and plan the closing around it.

More questions about Tooele County, UT Property Tax Guide

When are Tooele County property taxes due?

November 30 is the last day to pay current-year real property tax without penalty. Taxes become delinquent on December 1, and notices are mailed by November 1.

What is the deadline to appeal a Tooele County property valuation?

The deadline is the later of September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice was mailed. File with the county Board of Equalization, and bring comparable sales, an appraisal, a closing statement or proof of a factual error.

Do I lose the 45 percent residential exemption when I sell?

The seller no longer qualifies once the home is sold, and the new owner must apply on their own. Without an approved application the property can be taxed at 100 percent of market value.

Where is the Tooele County Treasurer?

The office is at 47 S. Main Street, Tooele, UT 84074, and the phone number is (435) 843-3190. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

Can you buy a Tooele County house with back taxes owed?

Yes, we buy houses with taxes owed. We get a current balance from the Treasurer and handle it through closing, and a house in any Tooele County town qualifies, from Tooele and Grantsville to Stansbury Park.

Who to contact in Wasatch County

Tax rate

Selling in Wasatch County?

Where is Wasatch County, Utah, and what is in it?

Wasatch County sits in north central Utah and is centered on Heber Valley, a mountain-ringed basin that is part of the Wasatch Back. It covers 1,206 square miles, of which 30 are water, and Heber City is both the county seat and the largest city.

Midway and part of Park City also lie inside the county line, along with smaller communities such as Center Creek and Soldier Summit. The county borders Salt Lake, Summit, Duchesne and Utah counties. More than half of its land sits above 7,500 feet, and the high point is on the west slope of Murdock Mountain in the Uinta Mountains at 10,840 feet.

The territorial legislature created the county on January 17, 1862, and chose Heber as the seat. The name comes from a Ute word that means a mountain pass. Its boundaries last changed on January 4, 1915, when the eastern portion became Duchesne County.

What do the Wasatch County numbers look like?

The county has a small population and has been growing quickly. These figures come from the Wikipedia county page, which cites the Census Bureau.

MeasureFigure
Total area1,206 square miles
2020 population34,788
2025 population estimate38,514
Population in 19808,523
Households (2020)11,040
Owner-occupied share of households76.3%
Median household income$85,807
Median age35.3

The 2020 count was 47.8% above the 2010 count. Read the July valuation notice closely each year, since it is the owner's first look at the new value.

What are Heber City and Midway like for a house owner?

Heber City is about 43 miles southeast of Salt Lake City, sits at 5,601 feet, and had 16,856 residents in 2020, up 48.4% from 2010. US 40 and US 189 both pass through it. Interstate 80 is roughly 18 miles north, and Interstate 15 is about 25 miles away through Provo Canyon.

About 27% of Heber City residents commute to Park City or Salt Lake City, according to Wikipedia. The largest local employer is the Wasatch County School District, and Wasatch High School, Timpanogos Middle School and Rocky Mountain Middle School are among its campuses.

Midway had 6,003 residents in 2020 and an elevation of 5,653 feet. Its Swiss-influenced building style is real enough that some subdivisions require a share of Swiss features on new houses. If you inherit or list a home there, ask about any subdivision design rules.

  • Homestead Resort in Midway has a geothermal pool used for year-round scuba diving.
  • Soldier Hollow offers cross-country skiing and a tubing hill.
  • Wasatch Mountain State Park lies on Snake Creek in north Midway.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wasatch County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How cold does it get, and what does that mean for the house?

Winters here are long and snowy, so a roof, a furnace and exterior pipes are the first things a buyer looks at. Heber City averages about 75 inches of snow a year over roughly 29 snowy days, with January and December the heaviest months at 21.5 and 17.8 inches.

The average January high is 36.5 degrees and the average January low is 12.5 degrees. The record low is minus 38. The average July high is near 89.5 degrees, and annual precipitation is about 15 inches.

None of this is a defect. It does mean that deferred roof, gutter or heating repairs on an older Heber Valley house are easy for an inspector to spot. If the house needs that work and you do not want to pay for it before selling, that is a common reason owners ask for an as-is cash purchase.

What drives the local economy around Wasatch County?

Tourism, public employment and commuting income hold up much of the county. The valley sits near three large reservoirs, Jordanelle, Deer Creek and Strawberry, and the county includes Deer Creek State Park, Wasatch Mountain State Park and parts of three national forests.

Wikipedia describes year-round visitor activity: skiing, snowmobiling, golf, off-roading, hunting and fishing, with Park City resorts nearby. Many adults work in Park City, Salt Lake City, Provo or Orem. Farming and ranching continue but have declined slightly.

The Heber Valley Railroad, the "Heber Creeper," runs on part of a line completed in 1899 between Heber City and Provo. Heber City Municipal Airport (Russ McDonald Field) is about two miles south of the city and gets very busy during ski season and the Sundance Film Festival.

Who runs property tax in Wasatch County?

The county assessor values property, the clerk/auditor sets rates and takes valuation appeals, and the treasurer collects the money. The county council also acts as the Board of Equalization, which hears appeals of value.

Utah assesses property at 100% of fair market value as of January 1. A home that you live in for 183 or more consecutive days in the year qualifies for a 45% primary residence exemption, per the county's own explanation. Qualifying farmland can be assessed on what it produces instead, and greenbelt applications are due May 1.

Utah's Truth in Taxation law, passed in 1985, made the system revenue-based. A taxing entity has to hold a public hearing before it raises the revenue it collects, and individual rates move when county-wide values move. For official detail, see the county's property tax system page.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wasatch County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What is the Wasatch County property tax calendar?

The calendar starts on January 1, the valuation date, and ends with the county tax hearings in December. The dates below come from the county's own schedule.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date
January 31Urban farming renewals due
May 1Greenbelt applications due
May 22Real property assessment roll closes
July 22Valuation notices mailed by the clerk/auditor
August 1 to September 15Board of Equalization accepts value appeals
October 30Tax notices mailed by the treasurer
November 30Payment due
December 1 to 31Hearings on tax increases for calendar-budget entities

How do you pay, and what happens if you are late?

Payments postmarked on or before November 30 carry no penalty. The treasurer takes online payments through Instant Payments and does not accept credit cards.

  • Payments received from December 1 through January 31 carry a 1% penalty.
  • Payments postmarked after January 31 carry a 2.5% penalty plus interest back to January 1.
  • Checks go to Wasatch County Treasurer, 25 N. Main, Heber City, UT 84032, with the parcel number written on them.

The office is open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The main line is (435) 657-3218. The treasurer's page also tells owners to confirm with their mortgage company whether it is paying the tax, which is easy to forget after a refinance or a loan sale.

The county posts a delinquent multiyear listing and updates it weekly. Interest keeps running, so the treasurer's office says payoff figures change daily and recommends calling (435) 657-3217 for the exact amount.

How do you appeal a Wasatch County valuation?

File with the clerk/auditor by 5 p.m. on September 15, either online or at 25 North Main Street in Heber City. State law sets the deadline as the later of September 15 or 45 days after the county gives notice, and the county board has 60 days to decide.

Evidence matters. The county says an application without evidence of your value estimate will be denied. You can group parcels in one appeal if they share an owner and sit in the same general area, but each parcel still needs its own proof. The clerk/auditor's number is (435) 657-3190.

If the board's answer disappoints you, the Utah State Tax Commission takes a further appeal filed within 30 days of the county decision, using Form TC-194 through the county auditor. The statute is Utah Code 59-2-1004.

How should you handle taxes when selling a Wasatch County house?

Get the payoff from the treasurer before you sign anything, then compare it with the closing statement. The weekly delinquent listing is the quickest way to see whether your parcel appears.

  • Pull the most recent tax notice and the July valuation notice.
  • Ask the mortgage servicer whether an escrow account has already paid this year.
  • Call (435) 657-3217 for the payoff on the day you plan to close.
  • If the house is empty or a seasonal home, update the mailing address so notices reach you.

If back taxes, deferred repairs or a second-home carrying cost are the reason you want out, we buy houses in Wasatch County as-is and can work around those problems.

More questions about Wasatch County, UT Property Tax Guide

How much is Wasatch County property tax due and when?

Payment is due November 30, and a payment postmarked by that date has no penalty. The county mails tax notices on October 30. The amount depends on your assessed value and the combined rate of every taxing entity that covers your address.

Does Wasatch County give a break for a primary residence?

Yes. Utah applies a 45% exemption to a home you occupy for 183 or more consecutive days in a year. The county asks owners to send residential exemption forms to the Assessor's Office before June.

When is the deadline to appeal my Wasatch County property value?

The county board accepts appeals from August 1 through September 15 at 5 p.m. Evidence of your own value estimate has to arrive with the form. File online or at the clerk/auditor's office at 25 North Main Street in Heber City.

Can I pay Wasatch County property tax by credit card?

No. The treasurer's office says it does not accept credit cards. You can pay online through Instant Payments, mail a check to 25 N. Main, Heber City, or visit the office on a weekday between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

Can I sell a Wasatch County house if the taxes are unpaid?

Yes, in most cases. Ask the treasurer for the payoff amount at (435) 657-3217, and have it paid from the proceeds at closing. We buy houses in Wasatch County as-is, so a tax balance does not stop us from making an offer.
